items.title: Cognitive-behavioral therapy in people with Parkinson's disease and caregivers: A mixed method systematic review on clinical applications and therapeutic outcomes

ai.headline: CBT may help depression in people with Parkinson’s disease, but evidence for other symptoms is weak.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 54 studies looked at cognitive behavioural therapy for people with Parkinson’s disease and their caregivers. Moderate-certainty evidence supports CBT for depression, while evidence for anxiety, sleep, impulse control, cognition, motor symptoms and caregiver outcomes is limited or very uncertain.

ai.caveat: The review includes studies of varying design and quality, and evidence for most outcomes beyond depression is low or very low certainty.

items.title: Socioeconomic Inequalities in Dietary and Physical Activity Behaviours Among Adolescents: A Systematic Review
items.venue: Journal of Human Nutrition and Dietetics

ai.headline: Teenagers from wealthier backgrounds tend to eat healthier diets and join more organised physical activities.
ai.summary: This systematic review looked at 38 studies on how socioeconomic position relates to adolescents' eating and activity habits. It found that higher socioeconomic position was linked to healthier diets, more fruit and vegetables, and more organised physical activity, while lower socioeconomic position was linked to poorer diet quality, skipping breakfast, and eating more ultra-processed foods.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that a young person's eating and activity habits are shaped by their family's social and economic circumstances, not just personal choice.
ai.life_skill: Notice how your local food options and activity opportunities might differ from those in other neighbourhoods.

quiz.answer: Associations with total physical activity and sedentary behaviour were inconsistent.

ai.caveat: Most included studies were observational, so they show links rather than prove that socioeconomic position causes these behaviours.

items.title: Effectiveness of home-based exercise interventions on cardiorespiratory fitness and cancer treatment-related cardiovascular toxicity in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
items.venue: Supportive care in cancer : official journal of the Multinational Association of Supportive Care in Cancer

ai.headline: Home-based exercise improves heart and lung fitness in cancer survivors treated with cardiotoxic therapies.
ai.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis looked at ten randomised trials involving 851 cancer survivors who had received cardiotoxic treatments. Home-based exercise programmes significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2 peak), but did not significantly improve six-minute walk distance or quality of life, and evidence on direct heart damage markers was limited.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that exercising at home may help cancer survivors maintain fitness after heart-harming treatments, though it cannot yet be said to prevent heart damage.
ai.life_skill: Try building regular home-based movement into your routine if you are recovering from cancer treatment, after checking with your care team.
ai.fact: Home-based exercise significantly improved VO2 peak by 2.35 mL/kg/min in cancer survivors exposed to cardiotoxic therapies.

quiz.answer: It significantly improved cardiorespiratory fitness, measured as VO2 peak.

ai.caveat: The review is based on ten trials and direct heart damage outcomes were assessed in only one study, so firm conclusions about preventing heart toxicity cannot be drawn.

ai.headline: Family difficulties are modestly linked to school refusal in children and teenagers.
ai.summary: A systematic review and meta-analysis combined results from studies on family factors and school refusal among children and adolescents. It found that greater family risk or lower family protection was positively associated with school refusal, though the strength of this link varied widely across studies.
ai.why_it_matters: It shows that family context can matter when understanding why a young person avoids school, without proving that family problems cause the refusal.

quiz.answer: Greater family risk or lower family protection was positively associated with school refusal.

ai.caveat: The evidence is mostly observational, so it cannot show whether family difficulties cause school refusal or result from it.

ai.headline: Active learning boosts grades, but more isn't always better once you pass a moderate level.
ai.summary: A rapid review of 58 studies looked at how much active learning university courses should use. It found that mid- and high-intensity active learning bring similar grade gains, both well above low intensity, while closing achievement gaps seems to need high intensity. ai.life_skill: Try mixing active tasks like discussion or problem-solving into about half your study time rather than only listening or reading.

ai.headline: Singing-based interventions may improve movement, voice, breathing, mood and quality of life in Parkinson’s disease.
ai.summary: A systematic review of 26 studies with 1057 people with Parkinson’s disease looked at singing-based interventions. ai.headline: Therapists say parent engagement in child therapy is shaped by barriers at parent, therapist and system levels, and a strong alliance helps.
ai.summary: Researchers interviewed 15 therapists about involving parents in their child’s psychotherapy. items.title: Implementation of WHO Self-Help Plus among Ukrainian university students during wartime: A multicenter longitudinal study

ai.headline: A five-week WHO self-help course reduced stress, anxiety and depression in Ukrainian university students during wartime, with benefits lasting three months.
ai.summary: Researchers studied 297 students with mild-to-moderate distress across five Ukrainian universities who took a five-week offline WHO Self-Help Plus course led by non-specialist facilitators. ai.why_it_matters: It shows that short, low-cost group courses run by trained non-experts can help young people cope psychologically during active conflict.
ai.life_skill: Try a short, structured self-help or coping-skills group if you are feeling stressed, and check whether your university or local health service offers one.
